name: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

validation.notes: Built from launch-week research. HUD positions are configurable in the game and were not checked against live captures; the recogniser reads what it can and leaves the rest out.

capture.notes: Borderless windowed mode captures most reliably. For the death map, set the minimap to fixed (not rotating) in the game's HUD settings.

modes.label: Private match vs bots only (no other players)
Multiplayer (core, Ground War, Gunfight, party modes)

playerContext.label: Your usual primary weapon (optional)
playerContext.help: Helps the coach talk about ranges and engagements that suit your loadout.

playerContext.label: Your minimap
playerContext.help: Death areas are only meaningful with a fixed (north-up) minimap.

vision.purpose: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (Multiplayer, DMZ or Campaign). Read the team scores and match timer if shown, the player's own kills and deaths only if shown (scoreboard or end-of-match screen), and what screen this is (lobby, loadout editor, map vote, loading, in match, killcam, scoreboard, after-action report). Detect when the player's own character dies (death screen, killcam of the player, respawn prompt) and, from the kill card or killfeed, what killed them. Detect the player's own kills only from a clear kill marker or a killfeed line with the player's name. The HUD can be moved (HUD bounds) and the minimap can be square or round, fixed or rotating; read what is there, guess nothing. On a killcam of the player's death, also read the fight: how exposed the player was, what they were doing, the range, who was higher, whether friendly dots were near on the death-screen minimap, and how many enemies engaged. Give unknown for anything not clearly visible.

state.label: Your team's score
state.description: The player's team score on the HUD or scoreboard. Omit if you cannot tell which side is the player's.

state.label: Time left (s)
state.description: The match timer converted to seconds, if shown.

state.label: Kills
state.description: The player's own kill count, only if shown (scoreboard, after-action report).

state.label: Deaths
state.description: The player's own death count, only if shown.

state.label: Current kill streak
state.description: The player's current streak counter on the scorestreak widget, if a number is shown.

state.label: Map
state.description: The map name, from a loading screen, map vote or scoreboard header.

state.label: Mode
state.description: The game mode name (e.g. Domination, Hardpoint), from a loading screen or scoreboard.

events.label: You died
events.description: The player's own character is visibly dead in this frame: death screen, killcam showing the player being killed, or respawn prompt.

attributes.description: The weapon class or source that killed the player, from the kill card or killfeed.
Only from the killcam or a damage indicator: where the shot came from relative to where the player was looking.
From the killcam: how much of the player's body the killer could see. in_open = nothing between them; partial_cover = edge of cover or head glitch.
From the killcam: what the player was doing when the first shot landed. sprinting = gun lowered in a sprint pose; aiming_still = aiming down sights and not moving.
Distance between killer and player in the killcam: close under ~10 m, mid ~10-30 m, long beyond.
From the killcam, relative to the player: you_lower = the killer was clearly higher than the player; you_higher = the killer was clearly lower.
From the death screen minimap: a friendly dot within a short sprint of the player, or none. unknown if the minimap is not visible.
From the killcam or the HUD at death: reload animation or empty magazine, throwing equipment, firing, or not firing.
From the killcam or damage indicators: one enemy engaged the player, or two or more.

events.label: You got a kill
events.description: A kill marker (e.g. '+100' with an elimination) or a killfeed line naming the player as the killer.

attributes.description: Distance to the enemy the player just killed, from the frame: close under ~10 m, mid ~10-30 m, long beyond. unknown if the target is not visible.
What the player was doing at the kill, from their own view: scope up and still = aiming_still.
Relative to the player: you_higher = the player looks down at the enemy; you_lower = the player looks up at them.

events.label: Killstreak earned
events.description: A banner shows the player earned a killstreak.

zones.label: Minimap area
zones.description: Divide the visible minimap into a 3x3 grid as drawn on screen (top = north on a fixed minimap). Use the player's own arrow at the moment of death. If the minimap is not visible or is rotating, give no zone.

concepts.title: Reposition after a kill
concepts.summary: Staying in the same spot after a kill gives the enemy a known place to challenge. A short move to new cover after each fight resets the angle in your favour.
good: Move a few metres to new cover after a kill
Reload behind cover
bad: Holding the same angle after it was revealed
Reloading in the open

concepts.title: Use the minimap
concepts.summary: Red dots on the minimap and the UAV show where fights are. Glancing at it between fights avoids running into crossfires.
good: Check the minimap after every engagement
Move toward your team's side of a fight
bad: Running across open lanes the enemy controls

concepts.title: Fight at your weapon's range
concepts.summary: SMGs and shotguns win close; assault rifles mid; snipers and marksman rifles long. Choosing routes that keep fights at your range wins more of them.
good: Take routes that suit your loadout
bad: Challenging a sniper lane with an SMG

concepts.title: Play the objective
concepts.summary: Objective actions build your streak too (Smart Streaks) and win matches. Capturing and holding often matters more than chasing kills.
good: Capture and hold in Domination and Hardpoint
bad: Ignoring the objective while the score slips

prohibitedAdvice: Positions of enemies that are not visible on the player's own screen
Exploits, glitches, or anything against Activision's rules
Anything that automates input or aiming

terminology.pre-aim: aiming where an enemy will appear before they do
terminology.trade: killing the enemy who just killed a teammate

items.name: Lanes and sightlines
items.detail: General Call of Duty map design (not checked per map): most core maps have three lanes; controlling the middle and avoiding long open sightlines with short-range weapons wins engagements.

playbook.title: Fight from cover
playbook.principle: Start every gunfight with most of your body behind something solid and a way out. Before each move, know where your next cover is if you get shot.
good: Shooting from a wall edge or doorframe
Crossing open ground only at full speed
Knowing your fallback spot
bad: Standing in the middle of a street or courtyard
Taking a fight with no cover in reach
signals: Killcam: your whole body visible, nothing between you and the killer
playbook.fix: Take fights only from the edge of cover you can step back behind.

sources.title: Advanced Call of Duty tips, Lineups

playbook.drill: Private match: walk each map and name the next cover from every lane.

playbook.title: Cross sightlines quickly, and rarely
playbook.principle: Long lanes are where held angles live. Cross them at the narrowest point, at full speed, ideally while your team draws attention or smoke covers you.
good: Sprinting or sliding across the narrowest gap
Crossing right after a teammate fires
Using different crossings
bad: Walking or aiming down sights across an open lane
Stopping mid-lane
The same crossing every life
signals: Killcam: long-range kill, you mid-lane side-on, the killer still
playbook.fix: Cross lanes fast at the narrowest point, or take a route that avoids the lane.

sources.title: How pros play Search and Destroy, EssentiallySports
Official Search and Destroy guide (MW III)

playbook.title: Know whether you are holding or pushing
playbook.principle: A player holding a pre-aimed angle usually beats the player walking into it. Hold an angle the enemy must cross, or push only with information, numbers, utility or timing on your side.
good: Holding a lane the enemy must use
Pushing right after a kill, a trade or a UAV
Utility thrown before the push
bad: Walking into a held angle with no information
Holding an angle nobody needs to cross
signals: Killcam: the killer stationary and already aimed where you appeared
playbook.fix: Push only with information, a numbers advantage or utility; otherwise hold.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Use head glitches and high ground; avoid fighting into them
playbook.principle: Cover that hides your body but lets you shoot over it, or a higher position, makes you a much smaller target. Challenging those spots head-on from low, open ground is a losing trade.
good: Ledges, boxes and sills that show only your head
Making enemies look up at you
bad: Standing in the open below someone who shows only their head
Re-challenging the same head glitch
signals: Killcam: the killer looks down at you, or only their head and gun clear the cover
playbook.fix: Do not fight into a head glitch from the open: flank it, throw utility, or take another route.

sources.title: What is a head glitch, GameFAQs

playbook.title: Do not peek the same angle twice the same way
playbook.principle: After a failed or spotted peek, the enemy pre-aims that spot. Change position, height or timing, or reset.
good: Wide swing, crouch peek or a different door after a failed peek
One quick look per peek
bad: Re-peeking the same edge at the same height within seconds
Dying twice to the same player at the same spot
signals: Two deaths in a row to the same killer at the same spot
playbook.fix: After one peek, change the angle, height or timing, or leave.

sources.title: Official Search and Destroy guide (MW III)

playbook.title: Move after you get a kill
playbook.principle: A kill gives away your position: a red dot if you are unsuppressed, plus a killcam for the player you killed. The next enemy comes to that spot.
good: Stepping back or shifting a few metres after the kill
Reloading behind cover
Pre-aiming where the next enemy will swing from
bad: Staying on the same angle and dying to the teammate of the player you killed
signals: Dying a few seconds after your own kill, at the same spot
playbook.fix: After every kill, move, reload in cover, then aim at the next likely entrance.

playbook.title: Play within trading distance
playbook.principle: Stay close enough that a teammate can kill your killer straight away, but far enough apart that one spray or grenade does not get you both.
good: A teammate covering your angle a few seconds behind
Trading kills
Never the lone player on a flank
bad: Far from every friendly dot
Stacked on a teammate and both killed together
signals: Death screen: no friendly dots near you on the minimap
playbook.fix: Stay one short sprint from a teammate who covers a different angle.

playbook.title: Do not sprint into likely contact
playbook.principle: After sprinting there is a delay before you can fire, longer after tactical sprint. A pre-aimed enemy wins that window, so slow down near corners and doorways with your gun up.
good: Releasing sprint before corners and doorways
Entering with the gun already up
bad: Rounding corners at full tactical sprint
Dying before the gun comes up
signals: Killcam: your gun lowered in a sprint pose when the first shot lands
playbook.fix: Stop sprinting before any corner or doorway that could hold an enemy.

playbook.title: Reload behind cover, not in the open
playbook.principle: A magazine usually holds more than one kill, so reloading after every burst wastes your safest moments. Reload when you are out of sight.
good: Checking ammo, stepping behind cover, then reloading
Switching to the sidearm if caught empty
bad: Reloading in the open right after a kill
A reload interrupted by the next enemy
signals: Killcam or HUD: reload animation or an empty magazine at the moment of death
playbook.fix: Reload only behind cover, or finish the fight with your pistol.

sources.title: Advanced Call of Duty tips, Lineups

playbook.title: Pre-aim common angles at head height
playbook.principle: Keep your crosshair where enemies will appear, at head height, so a fight needs only a small correction. Scump teaches this as centering.
good: Crosshair leading around corners at head height
Clearing one angle at a time
bad: Crosshair on the floor or a wall when you round a corner
Late flicks
signals: Killcam: you aimed away from where the killer appeared and turned only after being hit
playbook.fix: Before every corner, put your crosshair at head height where the enemy would appear.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.drill: Private match: walk each map pre-aiming every doorway.

playbook.title: Peek cheaply for information
playbook.principle: When you do not know if an angle is held, use a short jiggle, a mantle you can abort, or a quick slide peek before you commit. MW4 lets you steer and abort mantles.
good: A quick jiggle, then a committed swing
Aborting a mantle when you see an enemy
Utility before the peek
bad: A slow, wide peek into a held angle
Committing to a full mantle in the open
signals: Killcam: you died mid-mantle or during a slow, wide strafe into a lane
playbook.fix: Jiggle or abort the mantle to get information, then commit once you know.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Read the minimap every few seconds
playbook.principle: In MW4, red dots show when an enemy fires an unsuppressed weapon or your UAV is up. Firing unsuppressed puts you on their minimap too.
good: Glancing at the map every few seconds
Moving toward red dots from an unexpected angle
A suppressor when you want to stay hidden
bad: Dying to an enemy who showed as a dot seconds earlier
Firing unsuppressed from one spot and getting flanked
signals: Death screen: a red dot near the killer before you died
playbook.fix: Check the minimap before every corner and face red dots before they reach you.

sources.title: MW4 keeps the classic minimap, Dexerto
Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Play around UAVs
playbook.principle: With your UAV up, push with the information. With theirs up, assume you are seen unless you run Ghost, so stay near teammates and cover.
good: Pushing the moment your UAV goes up
Playing near teammates under an enemy UAV
Shooting it down
bad: Holding a lonely flank under an enemy UAV without Ghost
signals: An enemy UAV shortly before death, killer from behind or the side
playbook.fix: Under an enemy UAV, stay near teammates and cover or run Ghost; under yours, push.

playbook.title: Know where they will spawn
playbook.principle: Spawns depend on where both teams are. Pushing too deep, spreading out or wiping the enemy can flip spawns behind you.
good: Knowing the current enemy spawn
Holding angles that face it
Expecting a flip after a big push
bad: Chasing deep into their side
Getting shot in the back by freshly spawned enemies
signals: Killcam: the killer behind you, on the side your team held, early in their life
playbook.fix: After a wipe or a deep push, turn around, regroup and expect the spawns to flip.

sources.title: Rambo (CDL coach) on Ranked Hardpoint, Charlie INTEL

playbook.title: Take power positions as a team
playbook.principle: Rambo: Call of Duty is a game of positional warfare. Positions that see the most lanes and the enemy spawn exits create favourable fights.
good: Overlapping lanes toward the enemy spawn
A power spot held with a teammate
bad: Alone in a power spot with no trade
Leaving a power spot to chase kills
signals: Killcam: crossfire from two directions on a spot your team held
playbook.fix: Learn two or three power positions per map and take them with a teammate.

sources.title: Rambo (CDL coach) on Ranked Hardpoint, Charlie INTEL
Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Move with your team
playbook.principle: Solo rotations get isolated and lose fights one against two. Moving together lets you trade and take objectives.
good: Rotating with at least one teammate
Arriving at a new objective together
bad: Arriving first and alone
Dying before teammates get there
signals: Death screen: no friendly dots nearby; several enemies in the killcam
playbook.fix: Wait a second for a teammate before you enter a new area.

playbook.title: Fight at your weapon's range
playbook.principle: SMGs and shotguns win close, assault rifles win mid range, snipers and marksman rifles win long. Damage drops with distance, so fights outside your range are uphill.
good: SMG on short, close routes
Assault rifle holding mid lanes
Sniper holding long sightlines
bad: SMG fights across a long lane
A long gun in a cramped room against a shotgun
signals: Killcam: the killer far away while you hold an SMG, or close while you hold a sniper
playbook.fix: Pick routes that keep fights at the range your weapon is built for.

playbook.title: Shoot first, be ready first
playbook.principle: Whoever lands the first shot usually wins. Arriving pre-aimed, gun up and not sprinting decides most duels.
good: Seeing the enemy first through minimap or audio
Pre-aimed and firing on sight
bad: Reacting to being shot
Taking damage before your first shot
signals: Killcam: the killer fires first and keeps firing; your shots start late
playbook.fix: Arrive at likely contact pre-aimed, slower and with the gun up.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Hipfire close, aim at range, strafe
playbook.principle: MW4 removed hipfire bloom, so at point-blank range hipfire can beat a slow aim-down-sights. At range, aim before the peek and strafe while aimed.
good: Hipfiring a sliding enemy at a corner
Aiming before peeking a mid lane
Strafing while firing
bad: Aiming down sights at point blank and losing the race
Standing still while aimed in a long lane
signals: Killcam: you scoped in at point blank, or stood still while the killer strafed
playbook.fix: Hipfire within a few metres; otherwise aim before the peek and keep strafing.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Know when to leave a fight
playbook.principle: When you are hurt, outnumbered, out of range or empty, breaking line of sight beats finishing the fight.
good: Stepping back to heal after taking damage
Changing route after losing a long duel
bad: Re-peeking at low health
Chasing a damaged enemy into their team
signals: Killcam: low health at the start; chasing toward enemy teammates
playbook.fix: When hurt or outnumbered, break line of sight and reset.

playbook.title: Turn one-against-many into one-against-one
playbook.principle: When outnumbered, never let two enemies see you at once. Use spots where the second enemy must come through a door or around a corner.
good: Fighting one enemy at a time
Moving between kills
bad: Swinging into two enemies at once
Holding a spot two angles can see
signals: Killcam: two or more enemies in view, often a crossfire
playbook.fix: Pick spots where only one enemy can see you at a time, and move after each kill.

sources.title: Official Search and Destroy guide (MW III)

playbook.title: Do not swing when you are behind on numbers
playbook.principle: Swinging one against two in the open wins only when the enemies misplay. Wait for a teammate, utility or a better angle.
good: Checking friendly dots before you swing
Waiting for a trade partner
bad: Swinging alone into several red dots
signals: Several red dots near you before death; two damage sources
playbook.fix: When several enemies are near, wait for a teammate before you fight.

playbook.title: Hardpoint: rotate before the hill moves
playbook.principle: Hills follow a fixed order, so the next one is predictable. Rotating early wins the first fights on the next hill.
good: Some of the team leaving about 20 seconds early to set up
Fighting for the old hill only when it is worth it
bad: Everyone dying on the old hill, then running to the new one alone
signals: Death just after a hill change, at the new hill, with enemies already set up
playbook.fix: Learn the hill order and leave about 20 seconds early to set up on the next hill.

playbook.title: Hardpoint: break from every lane, then control spawns
playbook.principle: Rambo: hit the hill from every lane to get the break, then push between the hill and their spawn so they run through your positions.
good: Attacking the hill from several lanes at once
Holding between their spawn and the hill after the break
bad: Trickling in one by one through the same door
Everyone sitting on the hill
signals: Died entering the hill alone, or on the hill to an enemy outside it
playbook.fix: Attack with teammates from different lanes, then hold between their spawn and the hill.

sources.title: Rambo (CDL coach) on Ranked Hardpoint, Charlie INTEL

playbook.title: Domination: take B, hold two flags, keep spawns stable
playbook.principle: B is the key flag and two of three is usually enough. Pushing onto their home flag flips spawns and puts enemies behind you.
good: Taking B together
Someone covering home
Flipping spawns on purpose only after winning a big fight
bad: Three players running for their home flag
Chasing into their spawn and getting flanked
signals: Died near the enemy home flag, or from behind on the side your team held
playbook.fix: Hold B and your home flag; push their flag only right after winning a big fight.

playbook.title: Search and Destroy: avoid giving first blood
playbook.principle: In the 2020 CDL season, teams with first blood won 69% of rounds. One life per round means using the clock instead of rushing into a spectate.
good: Safe early angles
Trading teammates
Using the time to gather information
bad: Dry-peeking a common opening angle
Sprinting into a lane in the first seconds
signals: First death of the round, in the opening seconds, at a common angle
playbook.fix: Do not take the first fight of a round without information or a trade partner.

sources.title: How pros play Search and Destroy, EssentiallySports

playbook.title: Search and Destroy: share information and vary your play
playbook.principle: Dead players should call enemy positions. Change routes and holds each round; the enemy remembers where you were.
good: Calling positions after dying
Changing your hold each round
Smoke to cross long lanes
bad: The same route every round
Holding the spot where you got a multi-kill last round
signals: Died in the same spot as a previous round, to the same player
playbook.fix: Change your route or hold every round, and call what you saw when you die.

sources.title: Official Search and Destroy guide (MW III)
How pros play Search and Destroy, EssentiallySports
Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)

playbook.title: Read the killcam for the reason, not the excuse
playbook.principle: The killcam shows what the killer saw: whether you were in the open, sprinting, reloading, outnumbered, out of range or below them. Killcams are reconstructions and can be slightly off, so treat each read as probable.
good: Naming one cause per death
Looking for the same cause across deaths
bad: Blaming lag or luck
Skipping the killcam every time
signals: Your body in the open, a sprint pose, a reload, two enemies, the killer above you
playbook.fix: Watch each killcam for one thing you could have done differently.

playbook.title: Review your deaths and fix the most common one
playbook.principle: The cause you see most often is your current limit. Review deaths one at a time and work on one area.
good: Tagging each death by cause after a match
Practising the most common cause next session
bad: Trying to fix everything at once
signals: The same cause in most deaths of a match
playbook.fix: After each match, pick the most common cause of death and practise only that.

sources.title: Scump Teaches Pro Call of Duty Fundamentals (Aim Labs course)
MW4 keeps the classic minimap, Dexerto

playbook.drill: Theater mode: watch your deaths at half speed.

playbook.title: Learn the maps and the movement offline
playbook.principle: Positioning starts with knowing each map's lanes, spawns, power spots and hill order. MW4's movement (steerable, abortable mantles, the long slide) needs practice outside real matches.
good: Walking each map in a private match
Running the mobility course
bad: Learning maps only by dying on them
signals: Deaths in the same lanes across several matches on one map
playbook.fix: Walk each map in a private match and practise movement in the mobility course.

sources.title: MW4 launch maps and modes (official blog)

playbook.drill: Private match: name the lanes, power spots and spawns, pre-aiming every doorway.

limitations: Frames are sampled every 2–3 seconds, so fast deaths and kills can be missed; deaths are mostly caught on the killcam or death screen.
Death areas need a visible, fixed minimap; they are approximate.
Map, weapon and perk lists come from launch-week research; check them after patches.
Live tips only in the campaign and private matches with bots; everything online is reviewed after the match.

Fight details (cover, movement, range, height, support) are read from the killcam, which is a reconstruction and can be slightly off; findings are probable, not certain, and untagged deaths are counted, never guessed.
Kills are tagged only with what the player's own view shows (range, movement, height).
failClosed: No cloud vision: this pack cannot read the game.
Unclear whether the player or a teammate died: the event is not recorded.
